items.label: Written for 12MAG (Claude, modelled on Cambridge Example 19)
items.text: The number of bottles of sunscreen sold at a beach kiosk and the daily maximum temperature are linearly related, with r = +0.912. Determine the value of the coefficient of determination, write it in percentage terms and interpret. In this relationship, daily maximum temperature is the explanatory variable.
items.answer: r² = (0.912)² = 0.8317; 83.2% of the variation in the number of bottles of sunscreen sold can be explained by the variation in the daily maximum temperature.

items.label: Written for 12MAG (Claude, modelled on Cambridge Example 20)
items.text: Scores on tests of reading speed and spelling ability are linearly related with correlation coefficient r = +0.342. Determine the value of the coefficient of determination, write it in percentage terms, and interpret. In this relationship, reading speed is the explanatory variable.
items.answer: r² = (0.342)² = 0.1170; only 11.7% of the variation in spelling ability test scores can be explained by the variation in reading speed test scores.

items.label: Written for 12MAG (Claude, modelled on Cambridge Example 21)
items.text: For the relationship described by this scatterplot, the coefficient of determination = 0.6384. Determine the value of the correlation coefficient, r, rounded to four decimal places.
items.figure: scatterplot showing a moderate-to-strong POSITIVE linear association (draw when the slides are made; keep it positive)
items.answer: r = ±√0.6384 = ±0.7990; the scatterplot shows a positive association, so r = +0.7990.
